response.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT r.name, SUM(res.points) AS total FROM results res JOIN races r ON r.raceId = res.raceId GROUP BY r.name), a AS (SELECT AVG(total) AS avg_total FROM t), hi AS (SELECT t.name, t.total, a.avg_total FROM t, a WHERE t.total > a.avg_total) SELECT (SELECT SUM(total) FROM hi) AS combined_total_points, (SELECT AVG(CAST(res.laps AS REAL)) FROM results res JOIN races r ON r.raceId = res.raceId WHERE r.name IN (SELECT name FROM hi)) AS avg_laps_completed, (SELECT AVG(total - avg_total) FROM hi) AS avg_excess_over_average_total

assumptions.assumption: Race names are grouped by races.name, so all years of the same race name are combined. A race name's total is the sum of results.points over every result row with that name.
Average laps completed is the average of results.laps (cast from text to a number) over every result row in the above-average race names, so each driver entry counts equally.
The average total is the unweighted mean of the per-race-name totals across all race names. 'Above' means strictly greater.

alternatives.interpretation: Average laps completed is computed per race name first and then averaged across the selected race names, so each race name counts equally.
